1.why: All seven screens are static single-column forms with no animations, moving images, banners, or pop-up modals.

2.why: Bold headings, solid teal buttons, and the colored security notice stand out clearly, but the delivered token and confirmation code appear as unhighlighted plain-text lines inside the dark Logs block.

3.why: Each page shows one focused card with a single labeled input and button, though the codes she needs sit in a separate Logs section below the form rather than beside the relevant field.

4.why: Every screen states the next action and displays the needed codes on the same page, so the only rule set to hold in mind is the one-line password policy.

5.why: No 'remember me', password-manager, or autofill option appears on any screen; the inputs are bare fields with masked passwords and no show-password or manager integration.

6.why: The recovery-contact field starts empty with no saved contacts or familiar items to recognize, and only the timestamped Logs panel offers any reviewable history.

7.why: Core instructions are one or two sentences, but jargon such as 'non-identifying contact value', 'MFA', and 'mock delivery' plus a dense four-sentence security notice undermine plain reading.

8.why: No error state appears anywhere in the seven screenshots, so there is no observable evidence that error messages describe the problem and how to fix it.

9.why: No field shows a sample value or format (e.g., an example recovery contact or password); only procedural notes like 'You may paste or manually type the token' are provided.

10.why: The system offers no selectable authentication choices at all; the path is a fixed sequence of token, password, and code with no password/code/face-login alternatives presented.

11.why: Every screen presents exactly one input and one primary button, never multiple competing choices at once.

12.why: Each action ends in an explicit confirmation screen ('Sign-in confirmed', 'Privacy conditions accepted') plus a timestamped outcome entry in the Logs panel.

13.why: Each new step includes a one-sentence tip, such as where the six-digit code will appear and what the new password must contain.

14.why: No retry, resend, or error-recovery control is visible on any screen, and the footer's 'short-lived, single-use' token note implies a mistyped token cannot simply be tried again.

15.why: All seven steps reuse the same header, card layout, teal buttons, security notice, and Logs panel, so the design pattern stays consistent and learnable.
